timing: A separate training-only comparison registered after the first pair of native and proposed probabilities was seen. The sparse checkpoint assigned relation probability 0.00556 in that state. Retain the original rare-skill forecasts unchanged. Record any pre-existing relation writer or answer files at registration. Hold the first window out of the strict prospective report regardless of timing.
policy: Use balanced exploration as a reference, p=0.5. The source-only policy uses p=sigmoid(frozen source offset) in every window, retaining the earlier source scores, medians, interquartile ranges and signed offsets unchanged. Freeze all twelve probabilities without consuming any answers. Both rules use one common third-slot decision for all questions in the window.
evaluation: Reuse the same physically measured temporal and relation writer paths. Compare source-only to balanced, native, the original checkpoint-plus-affinity actor, fixed skills, and a constant matched to the source-only mean activity of the relation skill across comparable windows. Compute F1 per question, share skill usage per decision, and distinguish pre-existing or first-window scores from subsequent windows. This is a candidate screening experiment on six training dialogues.
